messages:
anya: Reopening a narrow slice of the on-prem upgrade RFC: delegation and authz for agents that perform staged apply in air-gapped sites. Need minimal, auditable primitives.

jules: Problem: operators sometimes want a support engineer to trigger fetch/activate without giving full admin keys. We need scoped tokens and expiry that are usable offline.

marco: idea: short-lived operator-approved challenge tokens. Operator runs `rwdctl grant-support --scope fetch,activate --ttl 24h` which prints a QR and base64 token. Support uses that token when connecting at site or when operator pastes it into a USB package.

sanjay: offline constraint: tokens must be verifiable without contacting central. So token should be a signed bundle: {scope, expires, nonce, operator_sig}. Agent verifies operator_sig against stored operator_pubkey fingerprint.

irene: UX tip: show token scope and expiry in preflight and require operator to type the token fingerprint to confirm. Also record which local actor created the token in `audit.jsonl`.

anya: extension: support-limited keys should map to agent RBAC roles: fetcher, verifier, activator. Agent enforces least-privilege: a fetcher cannot call activate. Tokens include role claims and optional `allowed_aliases` list.

jules: good. What about resume tokens for staged streaming? Current resume tokens are agent-signed and include blob offsets. We should make them bindable to an active support token so a fetched resume package can't be replayed by a different support actor.

marco: proposal: two-layer token model: operator-created support token (operator_sig) authorizes support actor; agent issues ephemeral resume token signed by agent key and including `authorized_support_token_id`. Resume token TTL short (hours) and single-use flag optional. Agent deletes resume state after use.

sanjay: security note: agent key material should be HSM-backed where available. For small appliances without HSM we allow software keys but require local policy to be stricter (shorter TTLs, more prompts). Document both paths.

irene: audit fields required for every auth action: ts, action, actor_id, token_id, scope, manifest_digest, result. Make it newline-json `audit.jsonl` for easy export.

anya: edge case: operator rotates their signing key. How does agent decide if a previously-created support token is still valid? Tokens include operator_pubkey_fingerprint and operator_id. Agent keeps a local mapping of trusted operator fingerprints and their validity windows. When operator rotates, they must publish a `rotation_notice` with overlap window or import the new pubkey prior to token issuance.

jules: include `rotation_hint` in support token optionally: {next_key_fp, start_ts}. If agent sees a token referencing next_key_fp before start_ts, it warns but can accept if operator explicitly allowed it.

marco: implementation note: token formats should be compact JSON then base64 URLsafe. Keep signature algorithm fixed to ed25519 for simplicity. Document fallback to rsa-pss only if HSM mandates.

sanjay: tests: simulate replay of resume token without matching authorized_support_token_id and ensure agent rejects. Also test expired and single-use semantics.

irene: UX microcopy: when operator runs `rwdctl grant-support`, CLI must print a one-paragraph warning that the token grants limited actions and is exported verbatim; suggest using USB transfer or ephemeral QR scanning; remind operator that tokens are audited.

agent-bot: NOTE: CI found flakiness in resume token single-use path (see job agent/authz/202).

anya: decisions to include in RFC patch: 1) support-scoped operator tokens signed by operator key; 2) agent-issued ephemeral resume tokens bound to support token id; 3) RBAC roles for agent actions (fetch, verify, activate); 4) audit.jsonl schema mandatory; 5) HSM vs software key policy documented with conservative defaults.

jules: +1 pending schema examples. I'll sketch the token JSON and CLI flow for the RFC.

marco: +1. I'll add unit tests and key-rotation simulations.

sanjay: +1. Will document HSM integration steps and fallback behavior.

irene: +1. I'll draft the UX prompts and audit samples for the PR.

anya: thanks all 1. I'll update the RFC branch with these authz primitives and sample token formats by EOD. If no objections in 36h we'll merge.
